children.prompt: The triangle is isosceles, with equal sloping sides.

spec.description: Symmetric-looking triangle with centred altitude, a full apex-angle arc crossing the altitude, and a right-angle mark at the foot. No equal-side ticks or angle-bisector marks are invented. Ordinary geometry uses black unfilled marks; a white mask keeps the apex label readable.
spec.mathematics: Full apex angle 70 degrees; right sloping side 30 cm; perpendicular altitude x cm. Isosceles status is not explicitly given.
spec.answerVisibility: The teacher answer 24.6 cm is omitted.

answer.worked:
The altitude of the isosceles triangle bisects the apex angle.
$\begin{aligned}\theta&=\frac{70^\circ}{2}=35^\circ\\\cos35^\circ&=\frac{x}{30}\\x&=30\cos35^\circ\\x&\approx24.6\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

children.label: i
children.prompt: The triangle is isosceles, with equal sloping sides. Find its area.

spec.description: Symmetric-looking triangle with centred perpendicular altitude and full 70-degree apex arc. Area request remains editable in the owning prompt. No equal-side ticks or angle-bisector marks are invented. Ordinary geometry uses black unfilled marks.
spec.mathematics: Full apex angle 70 degrees; right sloping side 30 cm; perpendicular altitude shown without a length. Isosceles status is not explicitly given.
spec.answerVisibility: The teacher answer 422.9 square centimetres is omitted.

answer.worked:
The altitude of the isosceles triangle bisects both the apex angle and the base. Let $h$ be the height and $b$ the whole base.
$\begin{aligned}\theta&=\frac{70^\circ}{2}=35^\circ\\\cos35^\circ&=\frac{h}{30}\\h&=30\cos35^\circ\\\sin35^\circ&=\frac{\frac{b}{2}}{30}\\b&=60\sin35^\circ\\A&=\frac12bh\\A&=\frac12(60\sin35^\circ)(30\cos35^\circ)\\A&\approx422.9\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$
